named_stops.linkedin: linkedin_paused_by_switch: owner_decision_2026-08-29: "drop linkedin for now its not important", and "i might bring linkedin back at anytime". LinkedIn is paused on purpose and is expected to come back. It is NOT off because LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN / LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN are missing from repository secrets -- that absence follows from this decision rather than causing it. This record exists so "paused by choice", "on but uncredentialled" and "on and posting" are three visibly different states instead of one blank secret. Nothing is posted and nothing is drafted -- this pause is dormant on purpose. Turn it back on by setting platforms.linkedin.enabled to true in data/social-brand-policy.json.
named_stops.x: x_paused_for_posting: owner_decision_2026-08-29: "im not funding X so find a $0 workaround or kill it." X's API is pay-per-use with no free tier -- every write this repository has ever made answered HTTP 402 problems/credits-depleted, starting with the very first request, and nothing has ever posted. At roughly $0.20 per post with a URL, eight a day is about $48/month. The owner has decided not to pay it. This is NOT a dormant pause: X is off for API POSTING only, and distribution continues by hand -- every scheduled run still writes the day's eight highest-value posts to reports/social-drafts.md, and she copies them out and marks the batch done in data/social-draft-ledger.json. That is what pause_mode "draft_by_hand" means and why it is not "dormant" like LinkedIn. ZERO requests were made to the x API this run. Distribution did not stop: the day's posts are on reports/social-drafts.md to be posted by hand, and marked done in data/social-draft-ledger.json. Turn automatic posting back on by setting platforms.x.enabled to true in data/social-brand-policy.json.
